Q: Limit Google Sheet to Only Be Viewed on a Tuesday (preferably between certain hours) A:

The manageTimeAccess() function is embedded inside myFunction() which makes it unreachable from many kinds of call methods, such as buttons, custom menu items or installable triggers.

To make the function testable, unwrap the manageTimeAccess() function by removing the initial function myFunction() { line and the trailing } at the last line.

Q: How to script a u-boot partition? A:

I would try to copy the complete /dev/sda1 from the working card to your "manual" card.

cp /dev/sda1 working-sda1.img
...
cp working-sda1.img /dev/sda1

If that works, you could check which files are different.
If it fails, check the MBR or copy it also from the working card

Q: Serial Commands for Mettler-Toledo FiveEasy Plus pH meter A:

I tried to achieve the same. I am able to get the data through RS (RS-USB cable) as you did, only by pressing read or automated version of the pH read. Putty can od it. Unless you construct a "pointing device" that will press read button this is it for RS. According to MT documentation the PC communication port is USB B. I managed to identify the instrument (alsoFiveEasy) through simple python script. USB B is not simple serial communication but HID. By pressing "read" in manual mode I can collect informations in time from the instrument but I do not know yet what commands to use to get actual data. Their EasyDirect software does not provide what I want. I want continues measurements instead of automated or manual reads after pressing button so hopefully continues measurement is possible. If not, I will just switch to other company that provides continues communication with the instrument. But USB B communication seems to be more productive for this.

Q: Receive UDP packets with python, packet loss A:

A few suggestions to improve your code, but first a question: have you measured at all what might be slowing things down? For instance have you looked at the CPU usage of your system. If you're hitting 100% that may very well the reason of the packet loss. If it's mostly idle, there is something else going on and the problem is not related to the performance of the code.

Now, some suggestions to improve the code:

  • use socket.recvfrom instead of sock.recv when dealing with UDP sockets
  • don't use multiprocessing with processes, the serialization that has to occur to send data from one process to the other may very well be a performance bottleneck if we're talking ~9000 calls/sec. Try to use threads instead (threading + queue modules). But as you're not providing any observed numbers it is hard to say really.
  • don't use string concatenation to build up the receiver's buffer as it gets packets. That creates large numbers of new temporary string objects and copies data around all the time. Instead, append each packet in a list and when you received all of the data, "".join(packets) them all together once at the end.

Q: Setup Mount Point in icecast server A:

Your Icecast server IP:Port listed are local; have you tested external to make sure you stream is accessible externally?

This is what you need to verify before testing anything else, making sure you Icecast2 server can resolve external requests on that port. Please make sure you edit your router's firewall with the ports you want to use e.g. 8001, 8002, etc.

"http://externalIP:port/mountpount" this is how you test external access in web browser

You can check out my Icecast streams at http://www.audiofraternity.uk and you'll see multiple streams (individual mount points for each DJ) I'm assuming this is what your trying to achieve but using IOS app for each DJ.
